newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen continuing to climb at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen continuing to climb at open.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open higher and enjoy another strong day on Thursday after a surge on Wednesday which took the exchange's key marker to its fifth straight record close.

"Yesterday's fifth record close and the Dow's break above 8000 is bullish...I don't think we're going to have as impressive a day as we had yesterday, but I think it is going to be positive," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said the slight weakness in bonds was to be expected after Wednesday's strong day and should not hurt stocks.

"Our long bond has broken 6.5 percent and that's bullish for the stock market for several reasons, the most important is at such low yields in the bond market there really is no place to put your money other than the stock market," Beattie said.
Canadian stocks and bonds strengthened yesterday on U.S. consumer price data which showed minor inflationary pressures on the U.S. economy.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index jumped 88.89 points on Wednesday to close at a new lifetime high of 6744.81. The key index also set an intraday high of 6746.18.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed past the psychological 8000 mark to close at 8038.
Beattie said stronger golds will also help Toronto stocks today. The Comex gold price was up US$1.50 per ounce to US$320.20 in early trade.
Analysts said slightly higher than expected Canadian consumer price data released earlier this morning was expected to little impact on the market.

"It still is at or below the Bank (of Canada's) point target of 2.0 percent for inflation control, so that's not a big deal," said Michael Gregory, economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers in Toronto.
Canada's unadjusted June consumer price index rose 0.1 percent in the month and 1.8 percent in the year, Statistics Canada said Thursday. Core CPI rose 2.0 percent year-on-year.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month.

* Suncor Energy Inc said today its second quarter per share earnings fell to C$0.26 from C$0.51 in the same period last year. Overall production declined in the quarter as a result of a planned 30-day maintenance shutdown at the Calgary company's oils sands facility, but the company said it is nevertheless on track to meet its goal of delivering a fifth straight year of improved financial results.

* Cominco Ltd said its second quarter earnings fell to C$0.20 per share from C$1.24 in the second quarter of 1996. It said the decline was principally due to the lower production of refined zinc at Trail as a result of the start-up of the new Kivcet lead smelter and slag fuming furnace.
